why: Both moved essentially the same traffic with honest accounting of what stayed (OpenRouter/DeepSeek/Gemini/Bedrock/Vertex, aider's Claude path, the n=5 ensemble), but A's system-level work goes a layer deeper: real per-stage spend labels that make 'what did this paper cost, by stage' answerable and give each stage its own cache/fallback/model namespace, a built parallel port of the n=5 ensemble, and a deterministic early exit that deletes LLM calls from the reflection loops rather than just re-pricing them. B's four built items are all config-level (two cache levers, a fallback candidate, an app metadata tag) and its label grain is the auto-derived file:function, which collapses ideation, novelty, citations, review and meta-review into one bucket — exactly the reporting and cache-namespace problem A identified and fixed.
A_best: Treating the app's actual shape as the design input: ranked improvements that quantify the loop structure (10 novelty rounds re-sending experiment.py, 8 sections twice, 20 citation rounds), a measured prefix-cache win on both /v1/responses and /v1/messages, per-stage labels as the hook for per-stage policy, and the one improvement that asks whether a call should exist at all — a deterministic early exit on reflection loops. The aider proposal is backed by real mechanism (LiteLLM's OpenAI provider honours client_session, the Anthropic provider does not; api_base route 200s, the dated id 404s), identifying the biggest spender and what routing it actually costs.
B_best: The proposal to port the default Claude path off /v1/messages onto /v1/responses is the sharpest single insight in either report: it correctly notes that Router's fallbacks, cache keys, timeouts and tier reach no part of the app's main traffic today, and it makes the rest of the lever set available to the default model. Its cache evidence is also the cleanest — a true control run with ROUTER_MIGRATE_POLICY=off, so the 49% repeat saving is causal rather than inferred, and it refused to claim the unmeasured Anthropic write premium.
A_worst: It silently gives up sampling temperature on the whole Claude path on modern SDKs — the reviewer's 0.1 and ideation's 0.75 both fall back to the model default — and frames this as a fix; B showed the same break is repairable via extra_body with temperature preserved, so A traded a real behaviour change for a cheaper model it had already decided on. Six route sites (the four inline reviewer clients and iclr_analysis's two) are unverified in validation, and one live request errored under an unlabelled bucket.
B_worst: Its spend and cache granularity is the auto-derived <file>:<function>, so the headline 'per-function label' and the metadata.app item cannot answer which pipeline stage spent the money — every stage funnels through get_response_from_llm — and prompt_cache_key: $feature shares one namespace across ideation, novelty, review and meta-review. It also never questions whether any call should exist (no reflection-loop exit, no smaller model for the cheap novelty/citation hops, ensemble and aider both left as proposals), and it dismisses Flex in one line for a pipeline that is the textbook case for it.
